toxicity.notes: Bark latex mildly toxic in large doses. Use under practitioner supervision.

Alstonia Scholaris.preparation: Bark decoction: boil 3g dried bark in 200ml water 10 min, filter, drink once daily. Never self-medicate.
Alstonia Scholaris.description: Saptaparni is one of the sacred trees of Ayurveda. Modern research confirms antimalarial and antibacterial properties.

toxicity.notes: Safe at recommended doses.

Arjun.preparation: Bark powder 1-3g with warm milk twice daily. Arjunarishta 15-30ml after meals.
Arjun.description: Arjuna is Ayurveda's premier cardiac herb, documented for 3000 years. Multiple clinical trials confirm cardio-protective properties.
contraindications: Consult cardiologist if on anti-hypertensives or statins

toxicity.notes: Fruit and leaves safe for all ages including children.

Bael.preparation: Dried fruit powder 5-10g with warm water before meals. Fresh sherbet: blend pulp with water and jaggery.
Bael.description: Bael's unripe fruit stops diarrhoea while ripe fruit relieves constipation — a unique dual action in plant medicine.

toxicity.notes: Safe for all ages. Avoid high doses in pregnancy.

Basil.preparation: Tea: boil 10 fresh leaves in 1 cup water 5 min. Drink 2-3 cups daily. Chew 4-5 fresh leaves on empty stomach.
Basil.description: Tulsi is the most sacred herb in Ayurveda. Used 5000+ years as a powerful adaptogen. Anti-viral, anti-bacterial, anti-diabetic properties confirmed.

toxicity.notes: Avoid inhaling dried leaf dust.

Chinar.preparation: Leaf decoction: boil 10g leaves in 400ml water, reduce half, strain. Use topically or drink 1 cup daily.
Chinar.description: Kashmir's iconic tree, used in Ayurvedic and Unani medicine for inflammatory and skin conditions.

toxicity.notes: One of the safest medicinal plants. Safe for all ages.

Guava.preparation: Leaf tea: boil 8-10 leaves in 1 litre water 10 min. Drink 1 cup 2-3x daily before meals.
Guava.description: Clinical trials confirm guava leaf tea significantly reduces post-meal blood sugar via alpha-glucosidase inhibition.
contraindications: Monitor blood sugar if on diabetes medication

toxicity.notes: All parts safe. Recommended dose for seeds.

ayurvedic_uses: Diabetes — converts starch not to sugar
Jamun.preparation: Seed powder: 1-2g with water twice daily 30 min before meals. Fruit: 10-15 daily in season.
Jamun.description: Jamboline specifically inhibits starch-to-sugar conversion. Validated in pharmacological research comparable to oral hypoglycaemics.
contraindications: Do not combine with insulin without monitoring

toxicity.notes: SEEDS HIGHLY TOXIC. External leaf use safe. NEVER consume seeds.

Jatropha.native_region: Tropical Americas, widely planted in India
Jatropha.preparation: EXTERNAL ONLY. Crush fresh leaves, apply to wounds 2x daily. Tiny latex on tooth cavity with cotton.
Jatropha.description: Important external medicine in tribal and Ayurvedic systems. Dangerous if seeds are ingested.

toxicity.notes: Completely safe.

Lemon.preparation: Fresh juice: half lemon in 200ml warm water on empty stomach daily. Peel tea: steep dried peel 5 min.
Lemon.description: Despite acidic taste, lemon has alkalizing effect in the body — documented in both Ayurveda and modern nutritional science.
contraindications: Undiluted juice erodes enamel — rinse after

toxicity.notes: Leaves and bark safe. Sap may irritate sensitive skin.

Mango.preparation: Leaf tea: soak 10-15 young leaves overnight in 400ml water, drink on empty stomach. Bark decoction for dental hygiene.
Mango.description: Mangiferin, unique to mango, has documented anti-diabetic, anti-viral and anti-cancer properties in clinical research.
contraindications: Ripe fruit: high GI — monitor if diabetic
Raw sap: contact dermatitis in some

toxicity.notes: Toxic to infants. Not internally in pregnancy. External use safe.

Neem.preparation: Skin: fresh leaf paste topically 20 min. Dental: chew twig end as toothbrush. Internal adults only: 1-2g powder with water, morning, 4-week cycles.
Neem.description: Called 'village pharmacy' — over 140 bioactive compounds. Antibacterial, antifungal, antiviral, anti-diabetic and anti-cancer properties confirmed.

toxicity.notes: All parts safe.

ayurvedic_uses: Highest antioxidant of any common fruit
Pomegranate.preparation: Fresh juice 200ml daily. Peel powder 2-3g with honey for digestive issues. Peel decoction as mouthwash.
Pomegranate.description: Punicalagins are converted by gut bacteria to urolithin A — one of the most potent anti-ageing compounds known.

toxicity.notes: Seeds mildly toxic internally. External skin use safe.

Pongamia Pinnata.preparation: Karanja oil: apply to skin 2x daily. Fresh leaf paste on wounds. Mix 1:4 with sesame oil for sensitive skin.
Pongamia Pinnata.description: Main ingredient in classical Ayurvedic skin formulations. Proven antifungal and antibacterial in dermatology research.

toxicity.notes: Safe for all ages.

Tulsi.preparation: Tea: 10 leaves in 1 cup boiling water 5 min. 2-3 cups daily.
Tulsi.description: Queen of Ayurvedic herbs. 5000 years of documented use. Anti-viral, anti-bacterial, anti-cancer confirmed.

toxicity.notes: Leaves and pods completely safe. Root bark internally: avoid.

Moringa.preparation: Leaf powder: 1-2 tsp in warm water or smoothie daily. Fresh leaves: cook as vegetable. Pods: cook in curries.
Moringa.description: Called 'miracle tree' — gram for gram more vitamin C than oranges, more calcium than milk, more iron than spinach.
contraindications: Root bark abortifacient — avoid in pregnancy

toxicity.notes: Safe at standard doses. Large doses may cause GI upset.

ayurvedic_uses: Stress and anxiety reduction — premier adaptogen
Ashwagandha.preparation: Root powder: 1-2g with warm milk and honey at bedtime. Ashwagandha churna: 3-6g with ghee and honey.
Ashwagandha.description: Ashwagandha is Ayurveda's most powerful Rasayana (rejuvenating herb). Clinically proven to reduce cortisol by up to 30% in trials.

toxicity.notes: Safe. Extremely long history of use with no toxic reports at normal doses.

ayurvedic_uses: 慢性的な熱とウイルス感染症
Giloy.preparation: Fresh stem juice: 20-30ml twice daily. Powder: 1-2g with honey. Kadha (decoction): boil 6-inch stem in 400ml water, reduce to 200ml.
Giloy.description: Called 'Amrita' (divine nectar) in Sanskrit. COVID-19 protocols in India included giloy for immunity. One of the most researched Indian medicinal plants.

toxicity.notes: One of the safest medicinal fruits. Safe for all ages.

Amla.preparation: Fresh fruit: eat 1-2 daily. Juice: 20ml with honey morning. Powder (churna): 3-6g with water. Chyawanprash: 1-2 tsp daily.
Amla.description: Amla is the foundation herb of Ayurveda. It is the first ingredient in Chyawanprash. The vitamin C in amla is bound to tannins making it heat-stable — unlike synthetic vitamin C.

toxicity.notes: Safe. Take with food to avoid nausea.

Brahmi.native_region: Indian Subcontinent — wetlands and marshy areas
Brahmi.preparation: Fresh juice: 5-10ml twice daily. Powder: 1-2g with warm milk. Brahmi ghee: classical Ayurvedic preparation for brain function.
Brahmi.description: Brahmi is Ayurveda's primary brain tonic. Clinical trials confirm significant memory improvement in elderly and in children with ADHD after 12 weeks.
contraindications: May slow heart rate — caution with beta-blockers

toxicity.notes: Completely safe. Widely used as food and medicine.

Hibiscus.native_region: Tropical Asia — widely cultivated in India
Hibiscus.preparation: Hair: blend fresh flowers with coconut oil, apply to scalp 30 min before wash. Tea: steep 3-5 dried flowers in hot water 5 min. Drink 1-2 cups daily.
Hibiscus.description: Hibiscus tea is clinically proven to lower blood pressure significantly. The flower is the primary hair care herb in Ayurveda.
contraindications: Blood pressure medications: additive effect — monitor

toxicity.notes: Completely safe as food and medicine.

Curry Leaf.native_region: Indian Subcontinent — tropical and subtropical regions
ayurvedic_uses: Anaemia (rich in iron and folic acid)
Curry Leaf.preparation: Fresh leaves: chew 8-10 on empty stomach daily. Tea: boil 15 leaves in 2 cups water. Add to all cooking for daily medicinal benefit.
Curry Leaf.description: Used in every South Indian kitchen, curry leaves are a functional food medicine. Daily consumption provides ongoing benefits for diabetes, hair and digestion.
contraindications: None known at culinary and medicinal doses

toxicity.notes: Unripe papaya and seeds can cause uterine contractions. Avoid in pregnancy. Ripe fruit completely safe.

Papaya.preparation: Leaf juice for dengue: extract juice from 2 fresh leaves, take 30ml twice daily. Ripe fruit: eat freely. Seeds: 1 tsp with honey as antiparasitic.
Papaya.description: Papaya leaf juice is a proven folk remedy for dengue fever, now supported by clinical studies showing significant platelet count increase.
contraindications: AVOID UNRIPE FRUIT AND LEAVES IN PREGNANCY
Blood thinners: papain has anticoagulant effect

toxicity.notes: All parts safe. Latex may cause contact allergy in sensitive individuals.

Jackfruit.preparation: Leaves: boil 10 fresh leaves in 500ml water, reduce to half, drink 1 cup daily for diabetes support. Raw fruit: eat as vegetable. Ripe fruit: eat freely as nutritious food.
Jackfruit.description: Jackfruit is the world's largest tree fruit and a complete nutritional food. The leaves have documented anti-diabetic properties. Young jackfruit is used as a meat substitute across South and Southeast Asia.
contraindications: Latex allergy: avoid if allergic to latex
Diabetes medication: leaf tea may lower blood sugar — monitor

toxicity.notes: Safe at normal consumption. High doses may cause caffeine-related effects.

Tea.preparation: Green tea: steep 1 tsp leaves in 80°C water (not boiling) for 2-3 min. Drink 2-3 cups daily. Avoid milk to preserve antioxidants.
Tea.description: Tea is the most consumed beverage after water globally. EGCG is one of the most potent natural antioxidants known. L-Theanine combined with caffeine produces calm alertness unique to tea.
contraindications: Iron deficiency: space 1hr from iron-rich meals

toxicity.notes: Completely safe. One of the most ancient medicinal plants in Ayurveda.

Sugarcane.native_region: New Guinea — cultivated in India for 4000+ years
Sugarcane.preparation: Fresh juice: drink 200-300ml daily. Add ginger and lemon for enhanced benefit. Jaggery (unrefined sugarcane): use instead of refined sugar for medicinal cooking.
Sugarcane.description: Sugarcane juice is one of Ayurveda's primary medicines for liver and kidney health. Jaggery (raw sugarcane) retains minerals lost in refined sugar processing.
contraindications: Diabetes: commercial refined sugar harmful, but fresh juice in moderation differs
